questions.stem: The galvanometer in a balanced Wheatstone bridge shows zero deflection. Which statement explains this?

questions.stem: How is the new position of a wavefront obtained from its previous position in Huygens' principle?

As the surface on which all the rays meet at a single focus point
As the locus of points where the path difference at two slits is zero
As the envelope of secondary wavelets from points of the old wavefront

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Sucrose is a non-reducing sugar. Which feature of its structure explains this?

options.text: Its glucose unit keeps a free aldehyde group at C-1, but it is sterically hindered
It exists only as the open-chain form of fructose, which is a non-reducing ketose
The glycosidic bond ties up both anomeric carbons, so neither ring can open to a carbonyl
It has no hydroxyl groups, so it cannot reduce Fehling's or Tollens' reagent

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: In the alpha-helix, the secondary structure of a protein is stabilised mainly by which interaction?

options.text: Disulfide bonds between the side chains of cysteine residues
Ionic bonds between side chains such as arginine and aspartate
Van der Waals forces between side chains of neighbouring helices
Hydrogen bonds between backbone C=O and N-H groups within the same chain

questions.subject: chemistry
questions.stem: Which reagents are used for the Wolff-Kishner reduction of a carbonyl compound to a methylene group?

options.text: Hydrazine, then KOH heated in ethylene glycol
LiAlH4 in dry ether, then aqueous work-up
H2 over Pd on BaSO4 with partial poisoning

questions.stem: In aqueous solution Cu⁺ disproportionates, while Cu²⁺ is stable. The main reason is:

options.text: The very high hydration enthalpy of Cu²⁺ outweighs the second ionisation enthalpy of Cu
The hydration enthalpy of Cu⁺ is larger than that of Cu²⁺ in aqueous solution
Cu⁺ has a half-filled d subshell, which makes it unstable in water
The second ionisation enthalpy of copper is lower than its first ionisation enthalpy
